title: Claude vs Codex on game development/modding
author: FunctionNice1887
selftext:
Been using codex for these tasks, 20$ plan and it’s worked amazing. But I keep hearing people talk about Claude, and I’m willing to try the 100$ plan if it gets me farther 

What’s the deal with Claude and what can it actually do over codex.

comments.author: h455566hh
comments.body: Use specialised AI apps, like bezi for unity, you'll get way better results.

replies.author: lostforever2011
replies.body: Surprised to hear that. You know anything liek that for unreal pls?

replies.author: AndreRieu666
replies.body: Have you tried unreal MCP in 5.8? I’ve been testing it, looks very promising.

replies.author: lostforever2011
replies.body: yes i plan to try that soon. i hope it good since i am not good with unreal :)

replies.author: AndreRieu666
replies.body: I’ve been using it the last 3 days or so, it’s actually quite capable.

replies.author: h455566hh
replies.body: Aura, yeah. And a couple of others.

replies.author: Spudly42
replies.body: How would this be better than Claude or codex?  You can already tailor your process to be game dev focused in those tools without much effort, plus you have full control over it.  You do need a unity MCP for the best results, but several of those are free and work with anything.

replies.author: khull123
replies.body: Why you're down voted? I tried coplay, bezi and aura, they provide most of the models at the same expense or even generous. I don't get the hate, if you are only game development focused.

comments.author: affabledrunk
comments.body: I use Claude at work and Codex at home for Game stuff. (100$ sub) and I find they are very comparable. I think you'll need the 100$ sub in both cases because you basically blow the 20$ weekly quota in like 15 prompts. I have yet to blow my 100$ weekly quota with codex, even after working for hours.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body:
Claude is more trustworthy on complex tasks, Codex is slightly stronger with visually focused tasks.

Both are capable but have different strengths. Personally I trust claude far more despite its lazy streak.

replies.author: Odd-Woodpecker-592
replies.body: Love that comment.  I agree that I trust Claude more but that's probably my biggest complaint about Claude Code in general these days.  I don't know if they've just started making it lazier.  I swear it wasn't so lazy when I started using it a year ago.

comments.author: John_Champaign
comments.body:
Start with the free tier for Claude, then upgrade to $20 if it's working for you and useful.  Then upgrade to the $100 plan if that's working for you and useful (and so on, and so forth).  I'm on the threshold of springing for Claude Max 20X.  I recently tried SuperGrok and it was definitely inferior to Claude Opus 4.8.  I used to use Codex, then tried Claude and found it better.

My feeling, generally, is that ChatGPT is better at images and Claude is better at coding.

comments.author: Happy_Variety5405
comments.body: I honestly use deepseek api, yeah it’s below Claude or codex in ability but it’s also 90 times cheaper and honestly haven’t found an issue it couldn’t solve

replies.author: camelovaty
replies.body: Deepseek you need to have insanely specific prompt...

replies.author: AndreRieu666
replies.body: What do you run it through to get a similar experience to Claude/Codex?

replies.author: Happy_Variety5405
replies.body:
I run it through Claude code cli, following the official setup: 
https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/agent_integrations/claude_code

comments.author: SubjectNo2985
comments.body: I'm using the max plan claude over powershell in Godot. I's working well. Full time opus model with xhight/ultracode and subagends. With optimize agent.md. For me, its much better then GPT. I using it for all my work. Automode and much more function i never found in GPT. So claude is my favorite.
